output.sql:
SELECT p.category,
       ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(l.net_amount) FILTER (WHERE o.order_date >= DATE '2024-01-01' AND o.order_date < DATE '2025-01-01'), 0), 2) AS revenue_2024,
       ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(l.net_amount) FILTER (WHERE o.order_date >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND o.order_date < DATE '2026-01-01'), 0), 2) AS revenue_2025,
       ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(l.net_amount) FILTER (WHERE o.order_date >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND o.order_date < DATE '2026-01-01'), 0)
           - COALESCE(SUM(l.net_amount) FILTER (WHERE o.order_date >= DATE '2024-01-01' AND o.order_date < DATE '2025-01-01'), 0), 2) AS revenue_increase
FROM marts.fct_order_lines AS l
JOIN marts.fct_orders AS o ON o.order_id = l.order_id
JOIN marts.dim_products AS p ON p.product_id = l.product_id
WHERE o.is_revenue
GROUP BY p.category
ORDER BY revenue_increase DESC
LIMIT 1
output.explanation: This returns the product category with the largest EUR increase from 2024 to 2025, with its revenue for both years and the difference. Revenue is the line net amount after discounts on completed orders only, excluding shipping. Years are based on order date. The 2025 figures include the 4% list price rise, so part of any increase reflects price rather than volume.
